skill.name: requesting-code-review

content.value_statement: Unreviewed changes can ship bugs, regressions, or incomplete requirements. This skill guides Claude, Codex, and Claude Code to request structured review before merge.
actual_capabilities: Guides users to capture base and head git SHAs before review.
Provides a code-reviewer subagent template for diff review.
Defines review categories for critical, important, and minor issues.
Checks implementation against requirements, tests, architecture, security, and readiness.
Recommends how to act on review feedback before continuing.
limitations: Does not run tests or commands automatically.
Requires accurate SHAs and requirement references from the user.
Review quality depends on available code context and diff scope.
Provides process guidance, not formal human approval.

use_cases.title: Review Feature Work
use_cases.description: Request a structured review after completing a feature, before the next task starts.

use_cases.title: Check Merge Readiness
use_cases.description: Use the checklist to confirm requirements, tests, and production concerns before merging.

use_cases.title: Coordinate Subagent Reviews
use_cases.description: Send a clear diff range and plan reference to a dedicated code-reviewer subagent.

prompt_templates.title: Review My Latest Change
prompt_templates.prompt: Request a code review for my latest completed task. Use the requesting-code-review workflow and ask me for any missing SHAs or requirements.

prompt_templates.title: Review Against Requirements
prompt_templates.prompt: Review the completed change against this plan: [requirements]. Check correctness, test coverage, and any missing requirement.

prompt_templates.title: Pre-Merge Readiness Review
prompt_templates.prompt: Before merge, review the implementation for production readiness. Categorize findings as critical, important, or minor, then give a clear merge assessment.

prompt_templates.title: Subagent Diff Review
prompt_templates.prompt: Use the code-reviewer template to review the git range from [base SHA] to [head SHA] against [plan]. Report strengths, issues by severity, recommendations, and readiness.

output_examples.input: Review a completed verification feature before continuing to the next task.
output_examples.output: The review lists specific strengths, identifies an important user feedback gap, notes a minor maintainability issue, and recommends fixes before proceeding.

output_examples.input: Check whether a change is ready to merge after a bug fix.
output_examples.output: The response compares the change to the stated requirement, separates critical and minor findings, and gives a clear merge verdict.

output_examples.input: Ask a subagent to inspect a diff range for test and architecture risks.
output_examples.output: The review summarizes architecture quality, flags missing tests where relevant, and explains why each issue affects production readiness.

best_practices: Provide the base SHA, head SHA, and requirement source before requesting review.
Ask for file and line references so every issue can be verified.
Fix critical and important findings before starting the next task.
anti_patterns: Requesting a vague approval without a diff range or requirements.
Treating minor style comments as blockers while ignoring real defects.
Continuing development after valid important findings remain unresolved.

faq.question: When should I use this skill?
faq.answer: Use it after completing tasks, major features, complex fixes, or before merging to main.

faq.question: Does it run the review automatically?
faq.answer: No. It provides the workflow and template for requesting a structured review.

faq.question: What information should I provide?
faq.answer: Provide what changed, the relevant plan or requirements, and the base and head SHAs.

faq.question: Can it work with Claude, Codex, and Claude Code?
faq.answer: Yes. The skill metadata lists support for Claude, Codex, and Claude Code.

faq.question: How should I handle critical findings?
faq.answer: Fix critical findings immediately, then request another review if the change is significant.

faq.question: What if the reviewer is wrong?
faq.answer: Respond with technical reasoning, point to code or tests, and request clarification.
